slides.title: High Availability and Architecture Considerations

rows: How quickly can it be restored?

blocks.title: High Availability and Architecture Considerations exam shortcuts
items: Example: Two app servers sit behind a load balancer.
Design for continued operation or effective recovery.
Example: Backup links keep service online.
Choose an architecture that can add or remove capacity.
Example: Cloud instances scale during peak traffic.
Example: An RTOS safety system reacts in milliseconds.
No practical patch path → INABILITY TO PATCH
Use compensating controls when updates cannot be applied.
Example: A legacy industrial controller cannot accept the patch.
Limited battery or CPU → POWER + COMPUTE
Example: A small IoT sensor cannot run heavyweight software.
blocks.example: Choose the architecture based on the security tradeoff emphasized in the scenario.

questions.q: A service uses redundant servers and automatic failover to minimize downtime. Which consideration is most directly addressed?
questions.explanation: High availability minimizes downtime through redundancy and failover.

questions.q: A company needs an architecture that can rapidly add capacity during peak traffic. Which consideration matters most?
questions.explanation: Scalability is the ability to grow or shrink capacity as demand changes.

questions.q: A controller must respond within a strict time limit. Which consideration is most important?
questions.explanation: Responsiveness focuses on latency and time-sensitive reaction.

questions.q: A legacy industrial system has a known vulnerability, but applying the patch would break production. Which consideration best fits?
questions.explanation: The system cannot safely accept the patch.

questions.q: A battery-powered IoT device cannot run a heavyweight security agent. Which considerations are most directly involved?
questions.explanation: Battery and processor limits are power and compute constraints.

questions.q: A company purchases cyber insurance to offset some financial consequences of a security incident. Which consideration is this?
questions.explanation: Insurance transfers some financial risk to another party.
